title: I Took the Blood-Bank Appointment Window to the Phlebotomist Who Double-Sat

parts.text: I had a 10:00 platelet window and at 10:04 someone else was already in my chair. The appointment screen the phlebotomist ran said: ONE CHAIR PER WINDOW. NO DOUBLE-SITS. I was thirty-four, regular donor, holding a barcode. Phlebotomist Kai said, "Walk-ins keep the machines busy." I pointed at the screen. Kai waved me to a folding chair. "Busy is medicine." I photographed the occupied chair, the screen, and my 10:00. Then I asked the charge to pull the chair log. At 10:08 the charge asked why Kai's name was on a double-sit ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The charge can see two bodies on one 10:00 window against Kai's own screen.

social.video_title: The chair was double-sat on my platelet window — Part 1/2
social.description: Barcode, a folding-chair exile, and a one-chair screen. I pulled the log. Would you have walked in later?

parts.text: Kai called it efficiency until the log showed my barcode first. I printed the ticket, the screen, and the photo. I sat. The walk-in waited. Kai told the lab the screen was always about optics. Optics is a word chairs use when a barcode exists. Window policy now has a second line: BUSY BOOKS A SECOND CHAIR. I donate. Kai queues walk-ins. The centrifuge finally has a name that matches.

social.video_title: Busy books a second chair — Part 2/2
social.description: Double-sit ticket, my window back, and a second line on the screen. Was medicine ever a folding chair?
